These contigs provide sequence representation and local-ordering of centromeric alpha satellite repeat monomers. The sequences are generated based on second-order Markov models of monomer variants, and graphical models of larger scale higher order repeats. The graphical models are based on an analysis of Sanger reads from the HuRef sequencing project (Assembly GCA_000002125.1; BioProject PRJNA19621), and their local-ordering is supported by observed same-read monomer adjacencies. The Markov models are generated by the program linearSat, which was written for this project and that also generates a linear representation of monomer order. The software linearSat generates a second-order Markov chain to the size of a given array provided by sequence coverage normalization estimates. The sequence definitions of transposable element insertions are limited to the sequences directly adjacent to alpha satellite within the read database, and incomplete representations are noted with an adjacent 100 bp gap. In total, these sequences provide a more complete reference of sequence composition and higher order repeat variation inherent to a given alpha satellite array, used to assemble centromeric regions of the human chromosomes.
DAAF01000000 has two assemblies built from the contigs: LinearCen1.0 (summed) and LinearCen1.1 (normalized). The original versions of the centromere records GK000035-GK000059 are part of LinearCen1.0, and the newer versions are part of LinearCen1.1.

bioprojects.title: Homo sapiens isolate:AK1 Genome sequencing and assembly

assembly_info.comments:
This is a de novo assembly of a Korean human genome. In the original assembly AK1_v1 (LPVO01000000) the initial contigs were generated using PacBio SMRT (single molecule real-time) sequencing long reads (101x) with error-correction by FALCON v. 0.3.0 and polished by Quiver. The polished contigs were compared with the genome maps assembled from BioNano Genomics next-generation map (97x) and corrected based on the reasoning that the next-generation maps provide longer structural information. The edited contigs were scaffolded with the genome maps. The resulting hybrid assembly was further polished with Illumina HiSeqX reads (72x), leading to the correction in long homopolymer regions. The genome map assembly and hybrid assembly were performed with IrysView v. 2.4.
This assembly, AK1_v2 (LPVO02000000), was generated by carrying out an additional round of scaffolding of the AK1_v1 sequences with a second set of genome maps assembled from BioNano next-generation map with fragile site rescue (108x).

assembly_info.comments: This is a partial *de novo* assembly of AK1 MHC region. To avoid misassemblies owing to hyperpolymorphic patterns of allelic variation, haplotigs for MHC class I and II were assembled independently after manual inspection for the haplotigs generated in AK1_Haplotigs_v1. In general, half of the reads phased as homozygous were used with reads phased as haplotype A to construct haplotig A, and the rest of the reads were assembled with reads phased as haplotype B to construct haplotig B, respectively. Homozygously phased reads flanked on each side of a sequencing gap belonged on each of the haplotype A and B, and were re-classified during assembly. Sequences MNPK01000001, MNPK01000005 and MNPK01000006 are haplotype A, and sequences MNPK01000002, MNPK01000003, MNPK01000004, MNPK01000007, and MNPK01000008 are Haplotype B.

bioprojects.title: Homo sapiens isolate:AK1 Genome sequencing and assembly

assembly_info.comments:
This is a de novo haplotype phased assembly of AK1 autosomes. Using AK1_v1 as a template, we built separate assemblies (haplotigs) representing the two haplotypes of each homologous chromosome pair. Phasing was performed with Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) long reads (101x), Illumina HiSeqX whole genome sequencing reads (72x), 10X Genomics linked reads (30x), and Illumina HiSeq2000 reads from BACs representing a single haplotype (47x). SNPs and indels called from the Illumina whole-genome sequencing reads were phased with linked reads into phasing markers. Afterwards, non-redundant set of PacBio long reads were classified according to the markers, and assembled with Canu v. 1.3. Reads in haplotype A plus homozygous regions were assembled into haplotig A and reads in haplotype B were assembled into haplotig B, similar to the alternate-loci of the human reference genome.
Sequences LYWJ01000001-LYWJ01003157 are haplotype A and sequences LYWJ01003158-LYWJ01018973 are haplotype B.

description.comment: Maternal Grandmother;donor subject is heterozygous for an A>C change at nucleotide 1061 (1061A>C) in exon 7 of the CYP2C9 gene (CYP2C9*3) which results in a substitution of leucine for isoleucine at codon 359 Ile359Leu (I359L);donor subject has a single bp (G-to-A) transition at nucleotide 681 in exon 5 of the CYP2C19 gene (CYP2C19*2) which creates an aberrant splice site. The change altered the reading frame of the mRNA starting with amino acid 215 and produced a premature stop codon 20 amino acids downstream;resulting in a truncated;nonfunctional protein. Because of the aberrant splice site;a 40-bp deletion occurred at the beginning of exon 5 (from bp 643 to bp 682);resulting in deletion of amino acids 215 to 227. The truncated protein had 234 amino acids and would be catalytically inactive because it lacked the heme-binding region.

assembly_info.comments: This is the November 2001 combined whole genome shotgun assembly applied to the 27 million reads of Celera's whole genome shotgun data and 16 million reads of shredded GenBank data from other human genome projects (Nature 2001. 409:860-921). It relied on Celera's paired reads and BAC end reads from TIGR for long range order and orientation. Its scaffolds were mapped to chromosomes using STS maps. For more detailed information about whole genome sequencing and Celera's assembly process, please refer to Venter, J.C. et al. Science 2001. 291:1304-1351.

attributes.name: title
attributes.value: DNA-seq of homo sapiens: adult male blood

attributes.name: design_description
attributes.value: For Hifi long-read sequencing of APR cohort samples, high molecular weight DNA was isolated from 200 L of flash frozen blood using both GenFind V3 and Nanobind DNA extraction kits per manufacturers instructions. For shearing, DNA concentration was first measured using Qubit 3 Fluorometerwith a dsDNA HS Assay kit (Thermo Fisher) and samples were adjusted to 30 ng/L in a total volume of 130 L. DNA samples were then loaded on Diagenode Megaruptor 3 hydropore-Syringe at a speed of 29 targeting 15-18 kb fragment length as recommended by the PacBio protocol. The sheared samples were run on 4200 Tapestation system to check the fragment length using Genomic DNA screen tape. SMRTbell libraries were prepared for sequencing using the SMRTbell Prep Kit 3.0. The libraries were attached to Sequel II primer 3.2 and Sequel II DNA polymerase 2.2 and sequenced on PacBio Sequel IIe equipment using SMRT cells 8M and Sequel II Sequencing kit 2.0. For each sample on Sequel 11e, three SMRT cells were used to produce at least 30x coverage. The runs were created to allow adaptive loading, 2h of pre-extension and 30h of movie times

attributes.value: For Hifi long-read sequencing of APR cohort samples, high molecular weight DNA was isolated from 200 L of flash frozen blood using both GenFind V3 and Nanobind DNA extraction kits per manufacturers instructions. For shearing, DNA concentration was first measured using Qubit 3 Fluorometerwith a dsDNA HS Assay kit (Thermo Fisher) and samples were adjusted to 30 ng/L in a total volume of 130 L. DNA samples were then loaded on Diagenode Megaruptor 3 hydropore-Syringe at a speed of 29 targeting 15-18 kb fragment length as recommended by the PacBio protocol. The sheared samples were run on 4200 Tapestation system to check the fragment length using Genomic DNA screen tape. SMRTbell libraries were prepared for sequencing using the SMRTbell Prep Kit 3.0. The libraries were attached to Sequel II primer 3.2 and Sequel II DNA polymerase 2.2 and sequenced on PacBio Sequel IIe equipment using SMRT cells 8M and Sequel II Sequencing kit 2.0. For each sample on Sequel 11e, three SMRT cells were used to produce at least 30x coverage. The runs were created to allow adaptive loading, 2h of pre-extension and 30h of movie times

description.comment: The CIMH-NP-3 PHP (pseudohyperphosphorylated) tau cell line is a derivative of the CIMH-NP-3 cell line. It was generated by lentiviral integration of a doxycycline-inducible gene cassette coding for a pathogenic 2N4R human tau protein containing the following mutations: S195Q, S199Q, S202Q, S235Q, S396Q, S404Q, S409Q, S413Q, S442Q, and Y231Q . The PHP tau protein can be overexpressed by adding 3 µg/mL doxycycline for 72 hrs. The parental CIMH-NP-3 cell line was generated from induced pluripotent stem cells, which were generated from human fibroblasts by Sendai Virus reprogramming. Fibroblasts were obtained at the University of Bonn, Germany in March 2008. Reprogramming occurred at the Central Institute of Mental Health in Mannheim, Germany in February 2018. CIMH-NP-3 (stable neural progenitors) were generated in Mannheim in May 2018. Lentiviral transduction occurred in Mannheim, Germany, in May 2019 (to obtain PHP and WT Tau cell lines). The subject was a healthy 33-year-old male volunteer who gave written informed consent. All experiments are in line with the Helsinki Declaration.

description.comment: We present the first reference-quality diploid genome assembly of the human embryonic stem cell line H9 (WAe009-A), one of the most widely used pluripotent stem cell models in developmental and biomedical research. This cell line, registered in the European and NIH Human Pluripotent Stem Cell Registries, has verified ethical provenance, ensuring its transparent and responsible use for human pluripotent stem cell research. Using high-coverage Pacific Biosciences and Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read sequencing, we generated a high-quality de novo assembly, phased it by integrating high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) data and validated it through multiple orthogonal methodologies. This assembly was coordinated by Simona Giunta of Sapienza University of Rome. PacBio HiFi and Hi-C sequencing was conducted by the Vertebrate Genome Lab (VGL) at the Rockefeller University, led by Erich D. Jarvis, Giulio Formenti, and Jennifer Balacco. ONT sequencing was conducted at the UC Santa Cruz Genomics Institute and Northeastern University. Assembly was completed by the VGL and Giunta Lab.
